name: evbuffer_launch_read_
prose: evbuffer_launch_read_(buf, at_most, ol), buffer_iocp.c:245-309 (Windows overlapped I/O), starts an overlapped WSARecv and returns 0 or -1 (r starts at -1). It returns -1 at once, before taking the lock, if upcast_evbuffer(buf) is NULL. Otherwise it takes the buffer lock and asserts that no write is in progress (EVUTIL_ASSERT aborts in debug builds). If buf->freeze_end is set or a read is already in progress it jumps to done and returns -1; no other fields were changed yet. Past that check it resets first_pinned and n_buffers and memsets the buffers array, which stays reset on any later failure. If evbuffer_expand_fast_(buf, at_most, MAX_WSABUFS) fails it returns -1. Otherwise it freezes the end of the buffer with evbuffer_freeze(buf, 0) (not the front), builds WSABUFs from evbuffer_read_setup_vecs_, records first_pinned and n_buffers, pins every chain from the first one onward with EVBUFFER_MEM_PINNED_R (asserting the pinned count equals nvecs) and takes an extra reference with evbuffer_incref_. If WSARecv fails with an error other than WSA_IO_PENDING it releases the pins, unfreezes the end, drops the reference with evbuffer_free and returns -1; otherwise (success or WSA_IO_PENDING) it sets read_in_progress = 1 and returns 0. The lock is released at done on every path after it was taken.

Old prose said the buffer is frozen 'at the front' and that early -1 returns have no side effects; evbuffer_freeze(buf, 0) sets freeze_end (buffer.c:3401-3409) and lines 265-267 modify buf_o before the expand step. evbuffer_expand_fast_ and the helpers not read.

name: dnsname_to_labels
prose: Static function dnsname_to_labels(buf, buf_len, j, name, name_len, table), evdns.c:1614-1678, encodes the dotted name into DNS length-prefixed labels in buf starting at offset j and returns the new offset (off_t) or a negative error. It returns -2 at once if name_len > 255. It then loops over labels: when table is non-NULL it first calls dnslabel_table_get_pos(table, name) with the remaining text from the current label, and if that finds a position it writes a 2-byte pointer (ref | 0xc000) (returning -2 via the overflow label if j + 2 exceeds buf_len) and returns j, without a terminating zero byte and without checking the length of any label in that remaining text. Otherwise it finds the next '.' (or the end of the name); a label longer than 63 bytes returns -1; a label that would not fit (j + label_len + 1 > buf_len) returns -2; otherwise, if table is non-NULL it adds the remaining text to the table at offset j (dnslabel_table_add), writes the length byte and the label bytes, and continues after the dot. In the -1 and -2 returns earlier labels may already have been written to buf and added to the table. After the last label it appends a zero byte when j is 0 or the last byte written is nonzero, with no bounds check against buf_len, so when the last label ends exactly at buf_len the zero byte is written at buf[buf_len] (one past the buffer). It then returns j, the offset just after the encoded name (or after the zero byte).

Reviewer round 1 RIGHT (terminating zero at line 1674 has no bounds check); round 2 RIGHT that the compression-pointer return at 1643 skips the zero byte (the old prose already said so); round 15 RIGHT (compression lookup at 1641 happens before any label-length check). dnslabel_table_get_pos and dnslabel_table_add were not read; that the table stores suffixes keyed by offset is taken from the call arguments.

name: evdns_base_set_option_impl
prose: Static function evdns_base_set_option_impl(base, option, val, flags), evdns.c:3484-3570, asserts the base lock is held (ASSERT_LOCKED) and returns an int: 0 or -1. It matches option against fixed prefixes: ndots:, timeout:, getaddrinfo-allow-skew:, max-timeouts:, max-inflight:, attempts:, randomize-case:, bind-to:, initial-probe-timeout:, so-rcvbuf:, so-sndbuf:. For each it parses val first and returns -1 on a parse failure, before looking at flags: strtoint (-1 if val has trailing characters; a literal -1 value is also indistinguishable from failure), strtoint_clipped (clipped to 1..255 for max-timeouts, 1..65000 for max-inflight), evdns_strtotimeval (-1 for trailing characters, a negative value, or a value under 1 ms, i.e. tv_sec == 0 and tv_usec < 1000), or evutil_parse_sockaddr_port for bind-to. After a successful parse, if the required flag bit is clear (DNS_OPTION_SEARCH for ndots, DNS_OPTION_MISC for the others, DNS_OPTION_NAMESERVERS for bind-to) it returns 0 without modifying the base. Otherwise it stores the value: ndots creates global_search_state with search_state_new if needed (return -1 if that allocation fails) and sets ndots; timeout, getaddrinfo-allow-skew and initial-probe-timeout (capped at 3600 s) copy the timeval into the base; max-timeouts, attempts (capped at 255), randomize-case, so-rcvbuf and so-sndbuf set the corresponding fields; max-inflight calls evdns_base_set_max_requests_inflight and ignores its result; bind-to stores the parsed address and length in global_outgoing_address/addrlen. An unrecognised option falls through and returns 0, as do all the successful cases.

Reviewer 'original' RIGHT (max-inflight result ignored at 3524; flag-gated no-op returns 0 at 3492 etc.); round 15 RIGHT (evdns_strtotimeval returns -1 for negative or sub-millisecond values, lines 3402-3406). search_state_new, evdns_base_set_max_requests_inflight and evutil_parse_sockaddr_port not read.

name: name_parse
prose: Static function name_parse(packet, length, idx, name_out, name_out_len), evdns.c:976-1030, decodes a DNS name starting at offset *idx of the packet into the NUL-terminated string name_out (labels joined by '.'), returning 0 or -1. It reads label length bytes through GET8, which jumps to the -1 exit if the read would pass length; a zero label ends the name. A length byte with either of the top two bits set (any value 64..255, not only 192..255) is treated as a compression pointer: it reads the next byte, records name_end as the offset after the first pointer (only the first time), sets j to ((label & 0x3f) << 8) + low byte, returns -1 if j is negative or at/after length, and returns -1 if the number of jumps exceeds length. Because of that test the later label_len > 63 check at line 1010 is not reachable. Otherwise a label is appended: a '.' is inserted before every label after the first (return -1 if no room), and -1 is returned if the label would not fit before the end of name_out (cp + label_len >= end) or runs past the end of the packet (j + label_len > length). On exit from the loop it returns -1 if cp >= end (not reachable when name_out_len > 0 given the earlier checks), writes the NUL, sets *idx to name_end if a pointer was followed, else to the offset just after the terminating zero label, and returns 0. *idx is modified only on the success path; on a -1 return name_out may contain a partial name. Packet reads stay below length and writes to name_out stay below name_out_len by the checks at lines 996, 1012, 1015 and 1016.

Reviewer round 1 RIGHT (label_len 64-255 takes the pointer branch at 998, so the check at 1010 is dead); round 15 WRONG (it says only 192..255 is a pointer; the test at 998 is label_len & 0xc0, true for 64 and up); round 2 'fixed-agree' no claim. The old prose was already right on this point; kept and tightened.

name: event_del
prose: event_del(ev), event.c:2786-2790, is a wrapper that returns event_del_(ev, EVENT_DEL_AUTOBLOCK). event_del_ (event.c:2768-2784) returns -1 without locking (after an event_warnx) if ev->ev_base is NULL; otherwise it takes the base lock (th_base_lock), calls event_del_nolock_(ev, blocking) and releases the lock, returning that result. event_del_nolock_ (2809-2898), run with AUTOBLOCK, returns 0 and does nothing else if the event has EVLIST_FINALIZING set (only EVENT_DEL_EVEN_IF_FINALIZING, which event_del does not pass, would delete a finalizing event). Otherwise it clears a pending signal-call count, removes the event from the timeout list, the active or active-later list and, if inserted, the inserted list and the evmap (evmap_io_del_ for read/write/close events, else evmap_signal_del_); a return of 1 from evmap is turned into 0 and requests a notify, and the result stays -1 if the evmap deletion failed. It also notifies the base (evthread_notify_base) when notify is set and res != -1 and the base needs notifying. With thread support, if blocking is not NOBLOCK and the event's callback is currently running in another thread (and, for AUTOBLOCK, the event lacks EV_FINALIZE), it waits on current_event_cond, which releases the base lock while waiting. It returns res (0 or -1).

Reviewer 'original' no longer applies (the prose already covers the NULL base -1); round 15 WRONG for event_del itself: event_del passes EVENT_DEL_AUTOBLOCK (line 2789), so the EVENT_DEL_EVEN_IF_FINALIZING exception at 2824 is not in effect and a finalizing event returns 0 undeleted. name: name##_HT_GROW(struct name *head, unsigned size)
prose: Generated function name##_HT_GROW(head, size), defined inside the HT_GENERATE macro (ht-internal.h:316-375) and instantiated for each hash table type. It returns 0 without changes if head->hth_prime_idx is already the last index, or if head->hth_load_limit > size. Otherwise it searches upward from the current prime index with do { new_len = PRIMES[++prime_idx]; new_load_limit = (unsigned)(load*new_len); } while (new_load_limit <= size && prime_idx < N_PRIMES); the loop test uses N_PRIMES rather than N_PRIMES - 1, so if even the last prime's load limit is not above size the next iteration reads PRIMES[N_PRIMES], one past the array; it does not simply fall back to the last prime. It then allocates new_len bucket pointers with mallocfn: on success it zeroes them, relinks every element into bucket HT_ELT_HASH_ % new_len, frees the old array with freefn if it was non-NULL, and installs the new array. If mallocfn fails it calls reallocfn(old table, new size), returning -1 if that also fails (head and its table unchanged), and otherwise zeroes the new tail, rehashes the elements in place, and installs the (possibly moved) array. After either allocation path it sets hth_table_length, hth_prime_idx and hth_load_limit to the new values and returns 0. Elements are not allocated or freed.
note: Slice 300-487 shows the HT_GENERATE macro body; HT_GROW read at ht-internal.h:316-375. Name is the generated name per the macro text. The old prose said the last prime is used 'if none does'; the loop condition at lines 330-331 permits an out-of-range index instead. Round 1 and 15 had no content claims (mechanical only).

name: name##_HT_CLEAR(struct name *head)
prose: Generated function name##_HT_CLEAR(head), defined inside the HT_GENERATE macro (ht-internal.h:378-384). If head->hth_table is non-NULL it calls freefn on it, then calls name##_HT_INIT(head), which resets the header to the empty state. It does not free head or the elements chained in the table (the caller keeps them). It returns void.
note: Read in full at ht-internal.h:378-384. The details of what HT_INIT writes (NULL table, zero lengths and counts, prime index -1) were taken from the old prose and from the condition in HT_REP_IS_BAD_ at lines 392-394; the HT_INIT definition itself was not read.

name: name##_HT_REP_IS_BAD_(const struct name *head)
prose: Generated function name##_HT_REP_IS_BAD_(head), defined inside the HT_GENERATE macro (ht-internal.h:387-420), checks the table header and returns an int diagnostic: 0 means consistent, nonzero means a problem. It does not modify head. If hth_table_length is 0 it returns 0 only when hth_table is NULL, hth_n_entries and hth_load_limit are 0 and hth_prime_idx is -1, else 1. Otherwise it returns 2 if hth_table is NULL, hth_prime_idx is negative or hth_load_limit is 0; 3 if hth_n_entries > hth_load_limit; 4 if hth_table_length differs from PRIMES[hth_prime_idx] (the index is not range-checked against N_PRIMES); 5 if hth_load_limit differs from (unsigned)(load*hth_table_length). Then it walks every bucket chain: for an element whose HT_ELT_HASH_ value differs from hashfn(elm) it returns 1000 + i (i the bucket index) for the first such element found; for an element whose hash modulo hth_table_length differs from its bucket index it returns 10000 + i; it counts the elements, and returns 6 if the count differs from hth_n_entries, else 0.
note: Read in full at ht-internal.h:387-420. The old prose's description matched the code; added the note that PRIMES is indexed without a range check at 404 and removed the claim that the first element found (in chain order) determines both 1000+i and 10000+i codes uniformly (they are returned in the order they are met).

name: main
prose: main(argc, argv) of the rate-limit test, test-ratelim.c:627-688. It initialises Winsock on Windows, seeds weakrand_state with evutil_weakrand_seed_, and on non-Windows returns 1 if signal(SIGPIPE, SIG_IGN) fails. It then scans argv[1..argc-1]: each argument is compared with the names in the options table; on a match handle_option is called and main returns 1 if it returns negative; otherwise it moves on (handle_option itself advances the index past a numeric value it consumed, and for boolean options just sets the flag without consuming a value). An argument that matches no option name prints "Unknown option" and usage and returns 1. handle_option (lines 580-607) returns -1 for a missing value, a value that does not parse fully as a decimal number, or a value below the option's minimum or above 0x7fffffff. A -h therefore does not stop later arguments being checked, and a later bad argument still returns 1. After the argument loop, if cfg_help is set it prints usage and returns 0, before doing any of the following. Otherwise it sets cfg_tick from cfg_tick_msec, sets seconds_per_tick and ratio to cfg_tick_msec/1000.0, multiplies cfg_connlimit and cfg_grouplimit by ratio, seeds srandom (srand on Windows) with the current microseconds, enables lock debugging unless thread support is disabled, and returns the value of test_ratelimiting().

name: handle_opt
prose: Static function handle_opt(opts, o_st), autoopts.c:101-203, applies one located option and returns a tSuccess value. It takes od = o_st->pOD and its handler opt_proc = od->pOptProc, frees od->optArg.argString if OPTST_ALLOC_ARG is set, and stores o_st->pzOptArg as od->optArg.argString; this happens before every later return, including PROBLEM. It returns PROBLEM if the options are being preset (OPTPROC_PRESETTING) and the option has OPTST_NO_INIT. If od has an equivalence class (optEquivIndex != NO_EQUIVALENT) it looks up the class descriptor eqv_od: if od already has OPTST_DEFINED and eqv_od->optActualIndex differs from od->optIndex it prints the "multiway bug" message to stderr and returns FAILURE; if od is not yet DEFINED it resets eqv_od->optActualIndex to NO_EQUIVALENT. When the class's actual index is not od's, it records od's value and index in eqv_od and sets OPTST_EQUIVALENCE in o_st->flags. It then copies od's argument string into eqv_od and continues with od = eqv_od. Without an equivalence class it sets od's optActualValue and optActualIndex. It then updates od->fOptState (keeping the persistent bits, adding the non-persistent o_st->flags) and, if that descriptor is DEFINED and ++optOccCt exceeds optMaxCt, returns too_many_occurrences(opts, od). Otherwise it calls the saved handler (*opt_proc)(opts, od) if it is non-NULL (note that od may be the equivalence-class descriptor by then) and returns SUCCESS.

name: optionPagedUsage
prose: optionPagedUsage(opts, od), pgusage.c:109-178, returns void. Without HAVE_WORKING_FORK it returns at once when od->fOptState has OPTST_RESET, otherwise it calls (*opts->pUsageProc)(opts, EXIT_SUCCESS) and returns if that returns. With a working fork it switches on the global pagerState. PAGER_STATE_INITIAL: returns at once on OPTST_RESET; otherwise it calls open_tmp_usage (which builds a temp file name from TMPDIR or the default dir and the pid, uses mkstemp under a restrictive umask, and returns NULL and frees the name if mkstemp fails) and stores the FILE* in option_usage_fp; if that is NULL it calls (*opts->pUsageProc)(opts, EXIT_SUCCESS) and, if that call returns, carries on with the following steps anyway. It then sets pagerState = PAGER_STATE_READY, saves print_exit in sv_print_exit, registers this function with atexit, sets print_exit = false, calls (*opts->pUsageProc)(opts, EXIT_SUCCESS) (which writes the usage text to option_usage_fp) and finally calls _exit(EXIT_FAILURE), so this case does not return normally. PAGER_STATE_READY (reached later through the atexit call): it builds the pager command with mk_pager_cmd(fil_name) (not read here, so whether it closes option_usage_fp is not stated), then, when sv_print_exit is set, writes "exit 0" to stdout, closes stdout and dup2s stderr onto stdout, else closes stderr and dup2s stdout onto stderr; it runs the command with system(), frees the command string with AGFREE and returns (the READY case falls through to the CHILD case's break). PAGER_STATE_CHILD does nothing and returns.

Reviewer 'original' RIGHT (open failure at 131-133 is handled by calling the usage proc, and the OPTST_RESET return at 129-130); round 15 RIGHT (open_tmp_usage failure calls pUsageProc at 133 before continuing). The old prose said the READY case closes option_usage_fp, which is not visible in this function (mk_pager_cmd not read). The pager state transitions elsewhere (e.g. the child state) not read.

name: optionResetOpt
prose: optionResetOpt(pOpts, pOD), reset.c:73-133, returns void and uses a static flag reset_active (initially false). It returns at once, leaving the flag unchanged, if pOpts <= OPTPROC_EMIT_LIMIT, and also returns at once without resetting anything if reset_active is already true (a re-entrant call), so the flag stays true on that path. If the originalOptArgArray is missing or originalOptArgCookie is NULL it calls ao_bug(zno_reset). If pOD->optArg.argString is NULL or empty it prints an error and calls pOpts->pUsageProc(pOpts, EXIT_FAILURE), followed by assert(0 == 1) if that returns. It then sets reset_active = true. If the argument is the single character '*' it calls optionResetEverything, sets reset_active = false and returns. For another single character it looks the option up with opt_find_short, and for a longer string with opt_find_long; if the lookup fails it prints an error, calls pUsageProc(EXIT_FAILURE) and asserts (reset_active stays true on that path). On success it calls optionReset(pOpts, opt_state.pOD), sets reset_active = false and returns.

name: dump_mac
prose: dump_mac(keyid, pmac, octets), digests.c:503-531, returns void and only reads pmac (bytes 4 to octets-1; the first four bytes are not printed). It starts a 128-byte local buffer with "digest with key %u { ". For idx from 4 to octets-1: when idx is 14 it first sends the current buffer to msyslog(LOG_DEBUG, "%s") and resets the write position to 0, so the bytes from index 14 on are written into the buffer from its start (without the header); then, if the write position is below sizeof(dump), it appends "0x%02x, " for pmac[idx]. After the loop, if the write position is below sizeof(dump) it appends "}", and it finally sends the buffer with msyslog(LOG_DEBUG, "%s"). So for octets <= 14 there is one log line (header, bytes 4 to octets-1 and "}"); for larger octets the first line holds the header and bytes 4 to 13, and the second line holds bytes 14 to octets-1 and "}", each only as far as the buffer holds (output is silently truncated by snprintf, and further appends stop once the position reaches the buffer size).
note: dump_mac read in full at digests.c:503-531 (the slice 513-532 started mid-function and was labelled a 'digest_dump fragment'; previously dropped, but this is a real function, so fixed under its real name). The old prose said the second line starts at pmac[15]; the loop at 515-524 writes pmac[14] into the reset buffer (line 520-523 run after the flush). msyslog not read.

name: gen_mvkey
prose: gen_mvkey(id, evpars), ntp-keygen.c:1554-1958, generates MV (mutual-verification) parameters and keys and returns an EVP_PKEY pointer. With n = nkeys it prints progress to stderr, allocates BIGNUMs and a DSA object, generates n distinct primes s1[1..n] of modulus2/n bits (retrying on duplicates, no bound on retries), forms q = product of the s1 and p = 2q + 1, regenerating one s1 at a time until p is prime (BN_is_prime_ex), then picks g with gcd(g, p-1) = 1 and g^q mod p = 1 (also unbounded retries) and stores p, q, g in the DSA. It chooses n zeros x[1..n] coprime to q, builds polynomial coefficients a[0..n] mod q, computes gs[i] = g^a[i] mod p, and runs a self-check: for every j it computes the product over i of g^(a[i] * x[j]^i) mod p (the code uses g and the exponent a[i]*x[j]^i, not gs[i]); if any product is not 1 it prints "Confirm ... no" and returns NULL immediately, before opening the key file or writing evpars, without freeing the BIGNUMs, DSA or BN_CTX. Otherwise it computes biga, a random group key b (coprime to q) and its inverse b1, the per-client keys xbar[j], xhat[j], the enabling key s, bige, gbar and ghat, opens the output file with fheader("MVta", "mvta", groupname), and writes three kinds of PKCS8 PEM keys through PEM_write_PKCS8PrivateKey: the trusted-authority key (assigned to the DSA, stored as evpars[0] and the value to return), the server key (a new DSA built from BN_dup copies) and n client keys, each stored in evpars in turn; for each client key it checks a relation and, if it is not 1, prints "Revoke key j" and continues (the key has already been written and stored). It terminates evpars with NULL, closes the file, frees a[i] and gs[i] for i in 0..n and x[j], xbar[j], xhat[j], s1[j] for j in 1..n, and returns the trusted-authority key evpars[0]. The remaining BIGNUMs (u, v, w, b, b1, s, biga, bige, gbar, ghat, p, q, g, priv_key, pub_key where not owned by a DSA) and the BN_CTX are not freed.
note: Real name is gen_mvkey (mv_param_gen does not exist in ntp-keygen.c); read the whole function at ntp-keygen.c:1554-1958 (slice 1578-1878 cut head and tail), skipping long comment blocks. Reviewer round 17 RIGHT: the self-check at lines 1738-1744 computes g^(a[i]*x[j]^i), not gs[i]^(...). The older prose otherwise matched (early NULL return at 1751-1752). BN ownership after DSA_set0_* calls (which BIGNUMs a DSA frees later) not analysed; the 'not freed' list is from reading the free calls at 1950-1956 only. fheader and PEM_write_PKCS8PrivateKey not read.

name: main
prose: Part of main(argc, argv) of the tg2 time-code generator (tg2.c main is lines 544-2188; this slice shows lines 1051-1313, so what follows describes that part and the exits seen elsewhere in main). After option parsing, main reads the system clock with gettimeofday and sets NowRealTime, BaseRealTime and SecondsPartOfTime from it, zeroes SecondsRunningSimulationTime and StabilityCount. If utc is set (option -y) the only assignment here is DayOfYear = ConvertMonthDayToDayOfYear(Year, Month, DayOfMonth): Year, Month, DayOfMonth, Hour, Minute and Second were already stored by the -y sscanf during option parsing. Otherwise it adds the signed UseOffsetSecondsInt to the seconds, uses gmtime to fill Minute, Hour, DayOfYear (tm_yday + 1), Year (tm_year % 100) and Second, and waits with delay(SECOND - tv_usec * 8 / 1000) to line up with a second boundary. It computes StraightBinarySeconds, clears code, and prints the starting point; for WWV it builds the code string from Year, DayOfYear, Hour, Minute and sets ptr from the program table, for IRIG it prints the legend when Verbose. Then it loops while SecondsToSend is 0 or CountOfSecondsSent < SecondsToSend: prints header lines every 20 seconds for IRIG, sets RateCorrection to -1, +1 or 0 from RemoveCycle/AddCycle, advances the leap-second state machine (NORMAL goes to DELETING at second 58 or INSERTING at second 59 when the date matches; DELETING sets Second 0; INSERTING sets Second 60; ZERO_AFTER_INSERT sets Second 0; any other LeapState prints a message and calls exit(-1)), increments Minute and Hour when Second wraps to 0, and applies the DST switch (Hour++ and offset adjustment for 'spring ahead', Hour-- for 'fall back') when DstSwitchFlag is set and the switch time matches; the slice ends inside that DST code. Later parts of main (lines 1320-2188, read only for their exit and return statements) build the output, may call exit(-1) on an unexpected FrameNumber (line 1590) or state-machine value (line 1793), do the rate-correction stability checks when EnableRateCorrection is set, and after the loop main prints "Completed %d seconds" and returns 0.
note: Partly read: main is 1,645 lines; I read lines 544-1320 in full (comments stripped) and for 1320-2188 only the exit/return/loop statements and a few contexts (1520-1545, 1586-1590, 1789-1793, 2045-2056, 2170-2188), so the encoding of the IRIG/WWV output second and the rate-correction logic are not described. Reviewer round 17 MIXED: lines 1060-1063 do set only DayOfYear in the utc branch, but Year/Hour/Minute/Second are set earlier by the -y option (line 854-855), so the old statement 'sets the starting values from the given UTC date' is right overall but this block alone sets DayOfYear. name: main
prose: Part of main(argc, argv) of the tg2 time-code generator (tg2.c main is lines 544-2188; this slice shows option cases 'l' to 'z' and the audio setup at lines 773-1050). If argc < 1 it calls Help and exit(-1); it sets CommandName, the default device and parses options with getopt (the option string includes "v:" only when HAVE_SYS_SOUNDCARD_H is not defined). Option 'l' sets UseOffsetSecondsInt from an hours value; 'o' sets the IEEE 1344 offset sign, ones and half bits; 'q' stores the low 4 bits of a hex quality; 'r' sets SetSampleRate; 's' increments leap; 't' sets tone = 1200; 'u' sets dut1 (absolute value if negative, else with bit 0x8 set); 'v' sets level, compiled only without HAVE_SYS_SOUNDCARD_H (with it, -v falls into the invalid-option case); 'x' clears Verbose; 'y' reads year, month, day, hour, minute, second and increments utc; 'z' sets Debug; any other option prints "Invalid option" and calls exit(-1). (The h, H and ? options call Help and exit(-1).) After parsing it forces Verbose on when Debug is set, computes LeapDayOfYear for a requested leap second and the DST-switch day and the pending-warning time one minute earlier (with hour/day/year borrow) when -g is given, and selects the encoding by tolower(FormatCharacter): 'i', '2', '3', '4', '5' choose IRIG variants and 'w' chooses WWV; any other value prints a message and calls exit(-1). It then opens the device O_WRONLY and calls exit(1) if the descriptor is <= 0. With HAVE_SYS_SOUNDCARD_H it sets mu-law, mono and the sample rate by ioctl and calls exit(-1) if an ioctl fails, if the format or channel mode comes back different, or if the rate differs from the request by more than 0.1%; without it, it calls AUDIO_GETINFO (calling exit(0) if that fails), fills in port, gain, rate, mono, 8-bit mu-law, prints them and applies AUDIO_SETINFO (result not checked). Execution continues after this slice with the time setup.

name: rcv_list
prose: rcv_list(sp), recover.c:495-592, lists recoverable files and returns 0 or 1. It returns 1 without a message if the O_RECDIR option is empty. It does chdir(O_RECDIR) and opendir("."); if either fails it queues a system error naming the directory and returns 1 (the working directory may already have been changed, and is never changed back, so on success too the process stays in the recovery directory). For each directory entry named "recover.*" it fopens the file (skipping it if that fails) and takes a lock with file_lock: LOCK_UNAVAIL closes the file and skips it, LOCK_FAILED and LOCK_SUCCESS both go on. It reads header lines with rcv_dlnread until both a "file" and a "path" entry are found; a nonzero return ends the file's processing, queuing the "malformed recovery file" message only when the status is 1. If stat on the recorded path fails with ENOENT it unlinks the recovery file by its entry name (an orphan, no output). Otherwise it fstat's the recovery file and prints "mtime: file" and sets found = 1. Each processed file is fclose'd (releasing the lock) and its file and path strings freed. After the scan, if found is 0 it prints "No files to recover"; it closes the directory and returns 0.

name: rcv_read
prose: rcv_read(sp, frp), recover.c:600-780, finds the newest recovery file for frp->name and starts recovery on it; it returns 0 or 1 and does not change the working directory. It returns 1 without a message if O_RECDIR is empty, and returns 1 after a system error message if opendir(O_RECDIR) fails. For each "recover.*" entry it builds the full path with join (a join failure queues a system error and skips the entry), fopens it (skipping on failure), and locks it: LOCK_UNAVAIL closes the file and skips the entry (the joined path is not freed on that path), LOCK_FAILED records locked = 0 and carries on, LOCK_SUCCESS records locked = 1. It reads the "file" and "path" headers with rcv_dlnread (a nonzero status ends that entry, with the 'malformed' message only for status 1), then increments found for every entry whose headers were read, including orphans. If the recorded path does not exist (stat fails with ENOENT) it unlinks dp->d_name, a bare name relative to the current directory rather than the recovery directory path, so the file in O_RECDIR is normally not removed; if the recorded file name differs from frp->name it is skipped; otherwise requested is incremented and, if this file is newer than the best so far (or the first), it becomes the selected recp/pathp with a dup of its descriptor in sv_fd (freeing the previous selection and closing the previous sv_fd). After the scan it closes the directory; if nothing was selected it queues "No files named %s ..." and returns 1. If found is nonzero it may queue 'older versions' (requested > 1) and 'other files' (found > requested) messages; since found counts orphaned files too, the latter can be shown when the other entries were orphans. It calls file_init(sp, frp, pathp, 0): on failure it frees recp and pathp, closes sv_fd and returns 1. On success it frees pathp, stores recp in ep->rcv_mpath and sv_fd in ep->rcv_fd, sets FR_UNLOCKED on frp if the chosen file was not locked, sets F_RCV_ON and returns 0.

prose: f_search(sp, fm, rm, ptrn, plen, eptrn, flags), search.c:144-276, searches forward for a regular expression and returns 0 on a match, else 1. It returns 1 if search_init fails. The start position is: with SEARCH_FILE line 1 column 0 (so a match can come before fm); otherwise it fetches line fm->lno with db_get (return 1 on failure) and uses, with SEARCH_INCR, column fm->cno (or fm->cno - 1 when that is nonzero) on the same line, else column fm->cno + 1, or, when that is at or past the end of the line, column 0 of the next line; if that next line cannot be fetched it returns 1 after an S_EOF message (only with SEARCH_MSG) unless O_WRAPSCAN is set, in which case it starts at line 1 with wrapped = 1. The scan loop checks for interruption every INTERRUPT_CHECK lines (break with rval 1; with SEARCH_MSG it calls search_busy, BUSY_ON then BUSY_UPDATE). When the line fetch fails or a wrapped scan has passed fm->lno: if already wrapped it breaks with S_NOTFOUND (only with SEARCH_MSG); else without O_WRAPSCAN it breaks with S_EOF (only with SEARCH_MSG); else it wraps to line 1. A line whose start column equals a non-zero length is skipped. It runs regexec on the rest of the line with REG_STARTEND: REG_NOMATCH continues with the next line; any other error calls re_error (with SEARCH_MSG) or the screen bell, and breaks with rval 1; on a match it issues S_WRAP if wrapped and SEARCH_WMSG is set (SEARCH_MSG is not required), sets rm->lno and rm->cno from the match (cno clamped to len-1, or 0, when SEARCH_EOL is not set and the column is at or past the line length) and returns 0 after the cleanup. name: re_sub
prose: Static function re_sub(sp, ip, lbp, lbclenp, lblenp, match), ex_subst.c:1300-1437, expands the replacement text sp->repl (length sp->repl_len) for one regex match into the line buffer *lbp and returns 0, or 1 on allocation failure. It works on local copies of *lbp, *lbclenp and *lblenp and appends characters with the OUTCH macro, which applies the pending case conversion (conv), may record a newline position for a CR or NL when newline translation is requested (growing sp->newl through NEEDNEWLINE, returning 1 on failure), and grows the buffer through NEEDSP (returning 1 directly from re_sub if the realloc fails; in that case nothing is stored back through lbp, lbclenp or lblenp). It scans the replacement: '&' copies the whole match when O_MAGIC is set; backslash handling: "\&" copies the match when O_MAGIC is not set, "\0".."\9" copy that submatch (offsets taken from match[0..9] against ip), "\e" and "\E" clear the conversion, "\l" and "\u" set a one-character lower/upper conversion, "\L" and "\U" set lower/upper conversion until cleared, "\<CR>" outputs the CR without newline translation, any other escaped character is output as itself, and a trailing lone backslash is output as a backslash. If the chosen submatch did not participate (rm_so or rm_eo is -1), nothing is copied and control falls through to output the selecting character itself ('&' or the digit). All other characters, and a '&' when O_MAGIC is not set, are output with newline translation. At the end it stores the buffer pointer, character count and allocated length back through lbp, lbclenp and lblenp and returns 0. The caller owns the (possibly reallocated) buffer.

name: s
prose: Static function s(sp, cmdp, s, re, flags), ex_subst.c:338-872, implements the ex substitute command and returns 0 or 1. NEEDFILE(sp, cmdp) returns early if there is no file; the original sp->lno and sp->cno are remembered. Unless O_EDCOMPATIBLE is set, c_suffix and g_suffix are cleared. If the argument string s is non-NULL it is scanned: '+' and '-' adjust cmdp->flagoff; a decimal count (allowed only once, else usage error) is read with nget_uslong, and any nonzero status returns 1 after "Count overflow", "Count underflow" or, for any other error, a system error message; a valid count sets addr1 to the old addr2 and moves addr2 forward by count-1, returning 1 if db_exist/db_last fail; '#', 'l', 'p' set print flags; 'c' toggles c_suffix (and initialises the text queue in ex mode); 'g' toggles g_suffix; 'r' returns 1 with a message if a regular expression was given (SUB_FIRST) or if there is no previous search RE (EXM_NOPREVRE), otherwise it uses sp->re_c; any other character, trailing characters, or a missing required 'r' (SUB_MUSTSETR) give a usage error and return 1. In vi mode the c flag combined with #, l or p returns 1 with a message. It then loops over lines addr1 (1 if addr1 is 0) to addr2 (which grows as inserted lines are counted), stopping on interrupt: it fetches the line (goto err on failure), runs regexec repeatedly (REG_NOMATCH ends the line; another error calls re_error and goes to err), handles empty matches, optionally asks for confirmation when c_suffix is set (answer 'n' skips the match, quit stops the loop), expands the replacement with re_sub (goto err on failure), and writes the modified line with db_set after inserting extra lines for any newlines with db_insert (goto err on failure), updating the changed-line count and printing the line with the l, # and p flags. After the loop, if sp->lno or sp->cno changed and c_suffix is not set it moves the cursor to the first non-blank of the current line. If nothing matched and the command is not inside a global command it queues "No match found" and returns 1; otherwise it sets rval 0 and, when something matched and none of l, # or p was given, sets E_AUTOPRINT on cmdp. Every goto err (and the no-match case) sets rval = 1. In all cases that reach the end it frees the temporary buffer bp and lb. Lines already changed before an error stay in the database.

prose: Static function ctag_sfile(sp, tfp, tqp, tname), ex_tag.c:1023-1154 (the packet name tag_search does not exist in this file), searches one tags file and appends matches to the tag queue; it returns 1 only on open, fstat or mmap failure and 0 otherwise. Otherwise it uses O_TAGLENGTH as tl, runs binary_search then linear_search for tname over the mapped text, and if linear_search returns NULL goes to done. It then loops over lines: a line is split in place (a NUL is written over the newline in the private mapping) into tag, file name and the rest; a missing field or empty search string queues "corrupted tag" and continues with the next line; a tag that does not match tname (strncmp over tl bytes if tl is nonzero, else strcmp) ends the loop; otherwise ctag_file resolves the directory and a TAG is calloc'd (CALLOC_GOTO jumps to alloc_err on failure), filled with the file name (prefixed by the tag file's directory unless it is '.') and a converted search string, and appended to tqp->tagq. If tqp->current is NULL and sp->frp->name equals the new TAG's file name, tqp->current is set to it. After the loop, if tqp->current is still NULL it is set to TAILQ_FIRST(tqp->tagq) (NULL if the queue is empty). Both the normal end and the alloc_err/done path then munmap and close (failures only queue a system error) and return 0; on allocation failure the TAGs already appended stay in tqp->tagq and the post-loop tqp->current assignment is skipped.

prose: Static function mark(sp, vp, getmark, cmd), v_mark.c:100-227, implements the ' and ` movements and returns 0 or 1. If getmark is nonzero it fetches the mark named vp->character into vp->m_stop with mark_get (return 1 on failure). For cmd == BQMARK it fetches the length of line m_stop.lno with db_get (return 1 on failure); if m_stop.cno is below the length (or both the column and length are 0) it stays a character mark; otherwise it sets VM_LMODE if the command is a motion and treats it as FQMARK. For FQMARK (and the converted case) it sets m_stop.cno = 0 and moves it to the first non-blank with nonblank (return 1 on failure). Any other cmd calls abort(). If the command is not a motion it sets vp->m_final = vp->m_stop and returns 0. For a motion: a BQMARK whose stop equals the start position calls v_nomove and returns 1; otherwise start and stop are swapped if stop precedes start, then m_final = m_start; an FQMARK motion returns 0 here. For a BQMARK motion, the end is made exclusive: if m_start.lno < m_stop.lno and m_stop.cno == 0 it moves m_stop to the end of the previous line (last character, or column 0 for an empty line; db_get failure returns 1) and sets VM_LMODE if m_start.cno is at or before the first non-blank (nonblank failure returns 1); otherwise it decrements m_stop.cno. After the swap this adjustment applies to whichever position is the later one, so for a backward motion (mark before the cursor) it moves the stop to before the original cursor position, not before the mark. On a return of 1 after the early assignments vp may already have been modified (m_stop from mark_get, VM_LMODE, the swap, m_final).

name: v_paragraphf
prose: v_paragraphf(sp, vp), v_paragraph.c:67-198, implements vi's } (forward paragraph) and returns 0 or 1. For a motion command it sets VM_LMODE if m_start.cno is 0; otherwise it sets m_stop to the first non-blank of the start line (return 1 if nonblank fails) and sets VM_LMODE if m_start.cno is at or before it. It then scans forward from line m_start.lno, counting blank and text runs (count doubled, minus one if the start line has text) with the INTEXT_CHECK macro (not read). When the paragraph boundary is found it returns 0 after setting: for a motion, m_stop to the last character of the previous line (lastlno) and m_final = m_start; for a non-motion, m_stop to (lno, 0) and m_final = m_stop. If a line cannot be fetched (end of file) it goes to eof: when m_start.lno is within one line of the failing line it calls db_eget on the start line; if that fails on a non-empty file it returns 1, and on an empty file it sets m_start.cno = 0 and returns 0 without setting m_stop or m_final; if the start column is already the last character it calls v_eof and returns 1. Otherwise (for a 'd' motion it sets VM_RCM_SETFNB after clearing the other RCM flags) it sets m_stop to the last line read at its last character (column 0 if empty) and m_final to m_start for a motion or m_stop otherwise, and returns 0.

name: v_paragraphb
prose: v_paragraphb(sp, vp), v_paragraph.c:206-306, implements vi's { (backward paragraph) and returns 0 or 1. For a motion command: if m_start.cno is 0 and m_start.lno is 1 it calls v_sof(sp, &vp->m_start) and returns 1; if m_start.cno is 0 on a later line it decrements m_start.lno and sets VM_LMODE; otherwise it decrements m_start.cno. If m_start.lno is then at most 1 (this applies to non-motion commands at line 1 too), or db_get of the original line fails, it jumps to sof, which sets lno = 1 and falls to found. Otherwise it scans backward line by line (count doubled, minus one when the start line has text; for a non-motion start with cno > 0 it first steps lno forward by one), using INTEXT_CHECK (not read) and blank/text transitions, and goes to sof if a line cannot be fetched. At found it sets m_stop to (lno, 0) and m_final = m_stop and returns 0. So its only return of 1 is the motion at column 0 of line 1; reaching the start of the file in other ways returns 0 with m_stop on line 1.

name: v_right
prose: v_right(sp, vp), v_right.c:29-71, implements vi's space/l command and returns 0 or 1. It fetches the length of line vp->m_start.lno with db_eget: if that fails because the file is empty it calls v_eol(sp, NULL) and returns 1; if it fails otherwise it returns 1 without calling v_eol; if the line length is 0 it calls v_eol and returns 1. It sets m_stop.cno = m_start.cno + count (the count when VC_C1SET is set, else 1); m_stop.lno is not set here. If m_start.cno is the last column (len - 1) and the command is not a motion it calls v_eol and returns 1. Otherwise, if m_stop.cno >= len it sets m_stop.cno = len - 1 and m_final to m_start for a motion or to m_stop for a non-motion; else for a motion it decrements m_stop.cno and sets m_final = m_start, and for a non-motion it sets m_final = m_stop. It returns 0 on those paths.

name: v_correct
prose: v_correct(sp, vp, isdelta), v_search.c:452-544 (the packet name search_adjust_tail does not exist), adjusts the start and stop marks after a search used as a motion and returns 0 or 1. If m_start and m_stop are the same position (search wrapped back to the start) it queues "Search wrapped to original position" and returns 1 with nothing else changed. If isdelta is nonzero it sets VM_LMODE in vp. It then swaps m_start and m_stop if m_stop precedes m_start, and sets m_final = m_start. If isdelta is nonzero it returns 0 here, so for isdelta the marks are swapped, VM_LMODE is set and m_final is set (vp is not unchanged). Otherwise, if m_start.lno < m_stop.lno and m_stop.cno == 0 it decrements m_stop.lno, fetches that line's length with db_get (return 1 if it fails, with m_stop.lno already decremented), sets m_stop.cno to the last column (0 if the line is empty), finds the first non-blank column of the start line with nonblank (return 1 on failure) and sets VM_LMODE when m_start.cno is at or before it; in every other case it just decrements m_stop.cno. It returns 0 after those steps.

name: v_sentencef
prose: v_sentencef(sp, vp), v_sentence.c:50-181, implements vi's ) (forward sentence) and returns 0 or 1. It initialises a character scanner at m_start with cs_init (return 1 on failure) and sets cnt to vp->count (VC_C1SET) or 1. If the first character is an empty-line marker or blank it skips blanks with cs_fblank (return 1 on failure); if the count then reaches zero it jumps to okret when the position moved from m_start, and returns 1 (no v_eof call) when it did not move. It then scans with cs_next (return 1 on error) in a state machine (NONE, PERIOD after '.', '?', '!', BLANK after following space or tab): end-of-file stops the scan; at an end-of-line the count is decremented when the state is PERIOD or BLANK, and on reaching zero it advances one more character, skips blanks and goes to okret; an empty line counts as two sentences; a space or tab after a period, or a second blank after BLANK, counts a sentence boundary and on reaching zero skips blanks and goes to okret. If the scan ends at EOF at the original position it calls v_eof and returns 1. At okret it stores the scanner position in m_stop. For a motion command: if m_start.cno is 0 and (the scanner flags are nonzero or m_stop.cno is 0) it moves m_stop to the last character of the previous line when m_start.lno < m_stop.lno (db_get failure returns 1; stop.lno stays decremented), and sets VM_LMODE; otherwise it decrements m_stop.cno; in both cases m_final = m_start. For a non-motion it sets m_final = m_stop. It returns 0 on those paths.

name: v_txt
prose: Part of v_txt(sp, vp, tm, lp, len, prompt, ai_line, rcount, flags), v_txt.c:237 onward (the packet name txt_istream does not exist in this file); this slice, lines 528-786, is the event-handling part of its input loop, so the following describes only that part. If vp has VC_ISDOT it jumps straight to replay; otherwise it fetches an event into ev at label next with v_event_get (return 1 if that fails). It redraws after filename completion when filec_redraw is set. It switches on the event type: E_CHARACTER continues; E_ERR and E_EOF set SC_EXIT_FORCE on sp and return 1; E_INTERRUPT, E_WRESIZE (after a message) and unknown events go to k_escape; E_REPAINT calls vs_repaint (return 1 on failure) and goes back to next. With TXT_RECORD set and nothing recorded yet, a NUL event goes to done if no replay buffer exists, else switches to replay mode (TXT_RECORD cleared, TXT_REPLAY set). When not quoting it tests for the cedit and filename-completion characters: cedit sets tp->term = TERM_CEDIT and goes to k_escape; the filec character calls txt_fc (goto err on failure) and goes to resolve. It counts abbreviation expansions (over 256 it flushes with a message and goes to done in replay mode, else to resolve). It records the event in vip->rep when TXT_RECORD is set (BINC_GOTO jumps to the error exit on allocation failure) and, in replay mode, takes the next recorded event (k_escape when the buffer is exhausted). It skips a space after a wrapmargin break, sends CH_QUOTED events to insq_ch, handles Q_VTHIS quoting by going to insl_ch for non-NL, and finishes a pending hex sequence with txt_hex (goto err on failure). For K_CR and K_NL: with TXT_CR set it records TERM_CR if the cursor is not past the offset, or TERM_SEARCH when running a search and the line has text, and goes to k_escape; otherwise (after LINE_RESOLVE expanding a pending abbreviation, which may go to resolve) it saves tp->sv_len/sv_cno, truncates the line at the cursor, updates the old line with vs_change, computes the text to carry onto the new line (skipping blanks for replace mode or autoindent), creates a new TEXT with text_init, appends it to sp->tiq, sets its insert, owrite and lno, and carries autoindent over with v_txt_auto. Failures of vs_change, text_init, v_txt_auto and allocation go to err.

name: bword
prose: Static function bword(sp, vp, type), v_word.c:403-522, implements the backward word movements (b and B) and returns 0 or 1. It sets cnt to vp->count (VC_C1SET) or 1 and initialises the scanner cs at m_start with cs_init (return 1 on failure). If the start character is not blank it steps back one character with cs_prev (return 1 on failure) and, if that character is also a non-blank, goes to start; otherwise it skips blanks backwards with cs_bblank (return 1 on failure). For type BIGWORD each of the cnt rounds moves back with cs_prev until a blank or other flagged position; in the other case it first classifies the starting character as in-word or not and moves back while the class stays the same. Every cs_prev, cs_bblank or cs_next failure returns 1; reaching the start of file (CS_SOF) jumps to ret. On the last round it steps forward again with cs_next (return 1 on failure) when the position is a normal character. At ret, if the scanner position equals m_start it calls v_sof and returns 1. Otherwise it sets vp->m_stop to the scanner position and vp->m_final = vp->m_stop, decrements vp->m_start.cno when the command is a motion, and returns 0.
